snippets.speakerTag: Two Garrison quartermasters, reconciling manifests
snippets.body: "Exchange numbers don't match ours again." "They never match. That's what a second ledger's for — so both sides can be right at the same time." "Harven doesn't see it that way." "Harven doesn't do inventory. Harven does decrees. Different skill.

snippets.speakerTag: Two traders under the leaning silo
snippets.body: "Still hasn't picked a direction." "Three years. I've got money down it falls east." "Everyone's got money down east, that's why it hasn't fallen east yet — this whole silo's just waiting to make somebody wrong on purpose." "That's not how buildings work." "You explain that to the silo."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Understory relay hands, striking the mast for the move
snippets.body: "You're moving it again." "Moving it is the whole point. A relay that sits still is just a target with a schedule." "Nobody's shot at it yet." "Nobody's found it yet. Those aren't the same sentence." "Seems like a lot of effort for three broadcasts a week that mostly repeat themselves." "Nobody's buying the message. They're buying proof somebody's still keeping a log that isn't the Garrison's and isn't the Exchange's. That's worth a coil of wire and a bad night's sleep."

snippets.speakerTag: Two pilgrims on the switchback trail
snippets.body: "Numbers were steady last time I read them." "Steady's not the same as good." "Steady's the only thing I've got faith is supposed to mean anymore. Good went out with the first winter." "Keep climbing. You'll feel better at the top." "I always feel the same at the top. That's rather the point of climbing, isn't it.

snippets.speakerTag: Two travelers waiting at the toll booth
snippets.body: "Rate's up again." "Rate's always up. Man's never once lowered it in three years, not even the season the road washed out and half his customers couldn't reach the booth." "Why do we still cross here, then?" "Because the other route takes a season and he knows it. That's not a toll, that's a tax, we just call it a toll so it feels like we agreed to it.

snippets.speakerTag: Two scavengers picking through the crater
snippets.body: "Rads are low right at the lip. Lower than the field around it." "Wrong way round. Should be hot at the point of impact, not scoured clean." "Maybe it wasn't meant to hurt anybody." "Everything out here's meant to hurt somebody. That's just the ones it's not aimed at talking.

snippets.speakerTag: Two clerks covering the empty counter
snippets.body: "Anyone taking his shift proper, or is it just us trading it back and forth?" "Just us. Nobody wants the counter he used to run. Feels like taking his coat off a body that isn't cold yet." "He'll turn up on a list somewhere. They always do." "Some of them don't. I've stopped assuming."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Weighbridge booth staff, watching an empty road
snippets.body: "Half of what used to cross here goes around now." "Around costs three extra days and people still take it." "Why?" "Because the long way doesn't run through a Garrison checkpoint asking where you're bound and why. We ask too, but we only ask it once, and then we let you through." "That's not much of a difference." "It's apparently the whole difference. We're not the toll anymore, we're the alternative to one. Never thought I'd call that a selling point."

snippets.speakerTag: A young roster member and an older trader
snippets.body: "Feels wrong, doesn't it. The coats." "Feels like three years of not needing them, ending on a Tuesday for no better reason than everyone else already stopped believing we didn't." "Adaeze hates it." "Adaeze hating it is the only reason I still trust it. The day she stops hating it, that's the day to worry."

snippets.speakerTag: A Garrison inspector and an Exchange trader, at the new post
snippets.body: "Weather's turning." "It's ash. It doesn't turn, it just falls slightly differently." "Trying to make conversation." "I know. I appreciate it, actually. Doesn't make the clipboard less of a clipboard." "No. It doesn't. Sorry about that, for what it's worth." "It's worth a little. Not nothing."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Garrison patrolmen off duty
snippets.body: "Fourth one this month I've had to write up as absconded rather than chase." "Why write up instead of chase?" "Because chasing means finding, and finding means deciding what happens next, and I've decided what happens next often enough for one war. Absconded's cleaner. For everyone, including him, probably."

snippets.speakerTag: Two children playing near the plaza's edge
snippets.body: "My mum says don't go past the rope they put up." "Mira gave her token away right before. To the radio lady." "Was it lucky?" "Mira says stars are only lucky if you don't need them to be. I don't think that's how luck works." "I don't think Mira thinks it's how luck works either. I think that's just what she says now.

snippets.speakerTag: Two shrine-keepers, after the anomaly
snippets.body: "Toma says we stop teaching the sparing." "Stop teaching it, or admit we never understood it?" "Does it matter, at this point?" "It matters to the pilgrims still climbing up here expecting an answer. It mattered to us three days ago too, before we didn't have one anymore."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Weighbridge booth staff
snippets.body: "Fennick's water deal holding?" "Held long enough for him to collect. Whether it holds for the slope's actual growing season is somebody else's arithmetic." "Doesn't bother you?" "Everything that crosses this bridge is somebody's arithmetic going wrong for somebody else. We just collect the toll on the crossing, not the consequences."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Forward Roster checkpoint watch
snippets.body: "First column paid without a word." "Word'll come. Give it a week, someone'll ask us who put us in charge of the road." "What do we tell them?" "Nobody. That's the whole answer. Nobody put us here. We just got here first and didn't leave."

snippets.speakerTag: Sella Krenn and a Forward Roster veteran, off the toll line
snippets.body: "Someone in that column called us bandits." "Bandits don't log the count." "We log the count." "Every crate, every head, in a hand that reads like a receipt. That's not a bandit, that's a customs post that opened early." "Doesn't feel like a customs post." "Nothing with a rifle slung ever feels like what it's doing on paper. Doesn't stop the paper being right."

snippets.speakerTag: Two D/9 cell operators, over the manifest
snippets.body: "Order says deny what can't be held." "Order was written before there was a checkpoint out there worth counting. Doctrine doesn't update itself." "So we update it." "So somebody above my clearance updates it. Until then I log the dissent and hold the line I was given, same as always." "That's not an answer." "It's the only one the manifest has room for."

snippets.speakerTag: Two pilgrims resting at the switchback waystation
snippets.body: "They still haven't repainted the board at the cairn." "What would they even write? The old line wasn't wrong for three years, and then one morning it was." "Toma won't say 'spared' anymore. I asked her straight and she just showed me the crater." "Can't blame her. Hard to keep teaching a word once you've stood in the hole it used to mean." "You think somebody was choosing what falls." "I think somebody was, for years, and now they're not, or they can't anymore. That's the part that keeps me climbing — I'd rather not have an answer than have the wrong one and build a shrine on it again."

snippets.speakerTag: An Exchange weigher and an upland farmer at the table
snippets.body: "Bag's damp at the corner. That's water weight, not rye." "Rye pulled out of the frost has dew on the husk, that's natural moisture." "Natural moisture doesn't pay the transit levy. We deduct four ounces for drying or you haul it back up the switchbacks." "Four ounces is robbery." "Four ounces is the rule since Tuesday. Robbery starts at six."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Garrison quartermasters, inspecting a stack of ordnance cases
snippets.body: "Wire's cut on this third one." "Cut or snapped?" "Clean shears. Snapped leaves a burr you can feel with your thumb." "Then someone took their four clips before the truck crossed the culvert." "Who do I bill for the seal?" "Bill the road. Harven doesn't inspect burrs; he inspects totals, and the total's short four."

snippets.speakerTag: Two allotment workers sitting on overturned soil buckets
snippets.body: "Take the thick heel of the bread." "I had the turnip end already. You take it." "I dropped it in the dirt anyway. It's half ash. Eat it before the wind steals the warmth." "Tastes better with ash. Cuts the bitterness."

snippets.speakerTag: Two haulers in the water queue
snippets.body: "Your bung's leaking into the drip trough." "It's just splash from the fill pipe." "It's grey water running back into the clean intake. Pull your barrel back before the supervisor sees it." "Supervisor's inside warming his hands on the steam pipe." "Doesn't mean his ledger's blind. Move the barrel."

snippets.speakerTag: Two relay technicians repairing a guy wire
snippets.body: "Hairline crack right across the ceramic bell." "Wrap it with vulcanized tape and haul it back up." "Tape won't stop fifty watts of RF arc when the frost melts." "Then keep the transmitter down at twenty watts." "Twenty watts won't clear the ridge into the valley." "It clears the ridge if nobody's running a diesel generator to jam it. Now tighten the turnbuckle."

snippets.speakerTag: Two Garrison patrolmen drying wool wraps by the hearth
snippets.body: "Left heel's giving again." "Grease it with tallow before you turn in." "Tallow's for the breech blocks now, Corporal says." "Corporal sleeps in the interior bunk with dry socks. Take the lard from the mess tin and don't tell the cook." "Cook knows already. That's why the soup tastes like harness leather."

snippets.speakerTag: Two scavengers inspecting a chalked railcar
snippets.body: "Mark says three crosses. That's Miller's crew." "Miller's crew hasn't been north of the Cut since the second blizzard." "Chalk doesn't wash off in snow. Mark's still dry." "Mark's on a rusted door with no hinges. Take the brake shoes and leave the axle. If Miller complains, he can carry the axle himself."

snippets.speakerTag: A master molder and an apprentice over a split casting
snippets.body: "Look at that scab. What did I tell you about the vent needle?" "I vented every two inches like the board says." "You vented two inches from the pattern, not the wall. Steam had nowhere to go but straight into the molten bronze." "Can we remelt it?" "Bronze takes coal, boy. Coal doesn't grow on slag heaps. Chip the sand out and ram it again."

snippets.speakerTag: Two merchants waiting on the ramp
snippets.body: "Three hours behind schedule. The team should have cleared the pass at dawn." "Axle grease froze in the hubs again. Happens every third cold snap." "You'd think after three winters they'd learn to cut the grease with kerosene." "Kerosene costs six chits a liter. Sticking in a snowdrift is free until someone starts shooting."

snippets.speakerTag: Two sentries huddled behind the sandbag berm
snippets.body: "Staff tent's got the blue heater going again." "You smell it from here?" "Paraffin smoke has a drift to it. You don't mistake that for coal." "Let them have the heater. Cold keeps a sentry from dozing off." "That's what they wrote in the manual so they wouldn't have to haul a second drum up the slope."

snippets.speakerTag: An operator and a log keeper by the transmitter board
snippets.body: "The 21:00 window was ninety seconds over." "The casualty names ran long. You want me to cut someone's kin off mid-syllable?" "I want the battery pack to last until midnight. Every second past the mark is plate voltage we don't get back." "Tell the battery pack that when the lists arrive."

snippets.speakerTag: A mother mending a glove while her boy spins a brass valve wheel
snippets.body: "What did the big wheel turn before the noise, Ma?" "Turned water into the basement heaters, sweet. Made the radiators clink in the morning." "Can it turn the water back on now?" "No, love. The pipe's broken under the street. Stop spinning it, you'll work the bolt loose." "I like the clink."

snippets.speakerTag: A melter and a pour hand watching the hearth
snippets.body: "Flame's pale straw. We're at temperature." "Billet team's still lining the ingot troughs with loam." "Tell them they have four minutes before the pot cools off. I'm not blowing another hour of bellows work because their shovels are cold." "They're coming. Don't drop the tongs."

snippets.speakerTag: Two traders examining stamped transit chits
snippets.body: "Garrison stamp is purple this month. Last month was green." "Means the old passes are scrap paper." "I've got forty bushels cleared under the green mark." "Then you sell twenty to pay for the purple mark, or you sit here until the snow melts and eat the difference."

snippets.speakerTag: Two camp guards tightening perimeter cord
snippets.body: "Line's dragging in the thistle again." "Wind caught the tin cans. Sounded like a patrol three times last watch." "Tie a stone to the dropper to keep the tension even." "Only got three stones left that aren't frozen to the clay." "Then chip one out. Better a sore wrist than an empty shoulder."

snippets.speakerTag: A roster sergeant and an orderly, over the slate
snippets.body: "Vane's got blood in his spit. He can't stand the cut watch." "He's marked fit on the morning roster." "He's marked fit because the pencil was in your hand, not because his lungs cleared." "Three posts are empty at the culvert. Either Vane stands there with his coat buttoned, or you take his carbine and stand there yourself." "I'll tell him to wear two shirts."

snippets.speakerTag: Two message runners checking a dispatch slip
snippets.body: "Is that a seven or a one?" "Graphite smeared when the condensation dripped off the pipe." "One means the cache is at the switchback; seven means the culvert." "Run the culvert first. If the charges are primed, you'll know it was seven." "Very funny. Hand me the dry sleeve."

snippets.speakerTag: Two laborers sorting scrap iron outside the kiln
snippets.body: "Inspector flagged the second rail bundle. Says there's sulfur inclusion." "Everything from the yard has sulfur. The coal was unwashed." "He says it won't weld for truss beams." "It'll weld fine for fence stakes. Stack it on the left and tell him it's for the perimeter ditch."

snippets.speakerTag: A transport driver and a fuel depot clerk
snippets.body: "Drum's two gallons light on the dipstick." "Sludge at the bottom takes up volume. Sits heavy as lard." "Sludge doesn't ignite in the injector, does it?" "It ignites if you heat the lines first." "You want me to build a charcoal fire under three hundred liters of diesel?" "I want you to sign the receipt so I can close the bay door before my tea freezes."

snippets.speakerTag: Two refuge stewards dividing supplies in a bus aisle
snippets.body: "Four wool blankets for six cots." "Double up the children. They generate more heat than the stove does anyway." "Mother's coughing into a rag." "Give her the canvas tarp over the blanket. Keeps the damp out. If we open another bale, there's nothing left for the next convoy."

snippets.speakerTag: An elderly homesteader scouring a soot-blackened pot by the stone wall
snippets.body: "Left flue first. Always the left flue, then the damper, then the ash drawer... No, three turns on the damper, Arthur said... Three turns and the smoke stays out of the larder. If you don't clean the throat, the frost gets in the flour. Always the left flue..."

snippets.speakerTag: A veteran rigger and an apprentice on the mast platform
snippets.body: "Always three wraps on the standing wire, then solder, then pitch." "Old man at the terminal just twists them and knots the cord." "Old man at the terminal has never climbed a hundred meters in a gale to find a loose joint buzzing like a hornet. Three wraps. Solder. Pitch."
